counts: People, and almost everything else
rule: The safety net. If you cannot remember the right measure word, say 个 — you will be understood.
trap: 个 is usually toneless (ge) when counting, not gè. Using 个 everywhere is safe but sounds childish for books (本), cars (辆) and flat things (张).

counts: Books, magazines, notebooks, dictionaries
rule: Anything BOUND at the spine takes 本.
trap: Do not use 张 for a book. 张 is for a single flat sheet; a book is many sheets bound, so it is 本.

counts: Flat things with a surface: paper, tables, beds, tickets, photos, maps, faces, cards
rule: If you can spread it out flat, it is 张.
trap: A chair is NOT 张 — it is 把 (it has a handle/back you grab). Beds and tables are 张.

counts: Long, thin, bendy things: trousers, skirts, roads, rivers, fish, streets, dogs
rule: Long and floppy → 条.
trap: A shirt (衬衫) is 件, not 条 — it is not long and thin. Trousers and skirts ARE 条.

counts: Upper-body clothes, and abstract "matters"
rule: Tops and troubles: 件 counts shirts, coats — and 事情.
trap: Never 件 for trousers or shoes. Trousers = 条, shoes = 双.

counts: Things that naturally come in twos: shoes, socks, chopsticks, hands, eyes
rule: Two of the same thing that belong together → 双.
trap: A single shoe out of the pair is 一只鞋 (只), not 一双鞋.

counts: Animals, birds, and ONE of a pair
rule: Furry, feathered, or half a pair → 只.

examples.pinyin: wǒ yǒu yì zhī xié zhǎo bú dào le
examples.en: I can't find one of my shoes

trap: 只 read zhī is a measure word; the SAME character read zhǐ means "only". The tone tells you which one.

counts: People you want to be polite to: teachers, guests, customers, managers
rule: The respectful 个. Use 位 for people you address politely.
trap: Do not use 位 for yourself or for children — it sounds odd. Use 个.

counts: People counted as members of a household (and some animals)
rule: Only for "how many people live in this home".

examples.pinyin: wǒmen jiā yígòng sān kǒu rén
examples.en: there are three of us in the family

trap: 口 does NOT replace 个 for people generally. 三口人 = family size; 三个人 = three people anywhere.

counts: Things you grab by a handle: chairs, umbrellas, knives, keys
rule: If your hand wraps around a handle → 把.
trap: 把 is also the famous 把-sentence particle (把书放在桌子上). Same character, completely different job.

counts: Vehicles with wheels: cars, bicycles, buses, taxis
rule: Wheels on the road → 辆. The 车 radical is right there in the character.
trap: Planes are 架 and boats are 艘/条 — not 辆. In HSK 3 you only need 辆 for road vehicles.

counts: Businesses and institutions: shops, restaurants, hotels, companies, hospitals
rule: A place with a "household" of staff → 家.
trap: 家 as a measure word never means "home". 我家 = my home; 一家商店 = one shop.

counts: Floors of a building, and layers
rule: Levels stacked on top of each other → 层.

examples.en: I live on the third floor

examples.pinyin: zhè zuò lóu yǒu shí céng

trap: 楼 also means floor (三楼). 层 counts them; 楼 names them. Both are used.

counts: School subjects and courses
rule: One door = one subject you walk into.

examples.pinyin: jīnnián wǒ yǒu wǔ mén kè
examples.en: I have five courses this year

trap: 门 as a measure word has nothing to do with real doors, even though the character is a picture of a door.

counts: Bus and tram route numbers
rule: The number of the bus line.

examples.pinyin: wǒmen kěyǐ zuò shí lù qù

trap: 路 here is not "road". 一条路 = one road; 10路 = the number 10 bus.

counts: Stops along a bus or subway line
rule: Count how many stops, not how far.

examples.pinyin: zuò dìtiě sān zhàn jiù dào le

trap: 站 is also the verb "to stand" and the noun "station". Context tells you which.

counts: Times something happens (occurrences)
rule: How many TIMES you did it → 次.

examples.pinyin: wǒ qù guo yí cì Běijīng
examples.en: I have been to Beijing once

examples.pinyin: zhège yào yì tiān chī sān cì
examples.en: take this medicine three times a day

trap: 次 goes AFTER the verb: 去过三次, not 三次去过.

counts: Times something happens (spoken alternative to 次)
rule: Everyday speech uses 回 where writing prefers 次.

examples.pinyin: wǒ qù guo yì huí Běijīng

trap: 回 is also the verb "to return" (回家). The measure-word use always follows a number.

counts: Yuan in speech; also lumps and pieces
rule: The spoken word for money, and for anything that comes in a chunk.

examples.pinyin: zhè běn shū sānshí kuài qián

examples.en: come and have a piece of watermelon

trap: 块 is spoken; 元 is written. A price tag says 30元, a person says 三十块.

counts: Yuan in writing (prices, receipts, bank forms)
rule: The formal, written unit of Chinese money.
trap: Never say 元 out loud in a shop unless you are reading a label. Say 块.

counts: One tenth of a yuan (written); spoken form is 毛

examples.pinyin: zhuōzi shàng yǒu wǔ jiǎo qián
examples.en: there is fifty cents on the table

trap: 角 is written, 毛 is spoken — exactly the same relationship as 元/块.

counts: One hundredth of a yuan; also minutes and exam marks
rule: The smallest unit: of money, of an hour, and of a score.
trap: 分 alone = minutes past the hour; 分钟 = a duration of minutes. 我等了三分钟 (I waited three minutes), 三点五分 (5 past 3).

counts: Kilograms
rule: 1 公斤 = 2 斤. Chinese markets use 斤 (500 g), forms use 公斤.

examples.pinyin: wǒ mǎi le yì gōngjīn jīdàn
examples.en: I bought a kilo of eggs

trap: 苹果两块钱一斤 means per 500g, not per kilo. Halve the price to compare with home.

counts: Metres
rule: The same character as "rice" — one metre of rice grains laid in a line.

examples.pinyin: zhè zhāng zhuōzi yǒu liǎng mǐ cháng
examples.en: this table is two metres long

trap: 米饭 is cooked rice; 米 alone in a measurement is always the metre.

counts: Years of age
rule: Only for how old someone is.

examples.pinyin: tā érzi jīnnián bā suì le
examples.en: his son is eight this year

trap: Never use 年 for age. 三年 = three years long; 三岁 = three years old.

counts: Bowlfuls of food
rule: The container becomes the counter.

examples.en: I'd like a bowl of noodles

examples.pinyin: wǒ chī yì wǎn jiù kěyǐ le
examples.en: one bowl is enough for me

trap: Containers double as measure words: 一杯茶 (a cup of tea), 一碗饭 (a bowl of rice), 一盘鱼 (a plate of fish).

counts: Cups and glasses of liquid
rule: The cup counts the drink inside it.

examples.en: please have a cup of tea

examples.pinyin: shuìjiào qián hē bēi niúnǎi ba
examples.en: have a glass of milk before bed

trap: 杯子 is the physical cup (a noun); 杯 without 子 is the measure word.

counts: Plates and dishes of food
rule: Like 碗, the dish counts what is on it.

examples.en: there is fish on the plate

trap: 盘子 = the object; 盘 = the measure word.

counts: Kinds, sorts, types
rule: Not "how many" but "how many different kinds".

examples.zh: 超市里有很多种新鲜水果
examples.pinyin: chāoshì lǐ yǒu hěn duō zhǒng xīnxiān shuǐguǒ
examples.en: the supermarket has many kinds of fresh fruit

trap: 种 read zhòng is the verb "to plant". As a measure word it is always zhǒng (third tone).

counts: Stretches: of writing, of time, of road
rule: A section cut out of something longer.

examples.pinyin: zhè duàn shíjiān wǒ hěn máng
examples.en: I've been busy during this period

trap: 段 is for stretches, 条 for the whole long thing: 一条路 (one road) vs 一段路 (a stretch of road).

counts: An unspecified small number — "some"
rule: Always follows 一/这/那 and never takes a number bigger than one.
trap: You cannot say 三些. Only 一些, 这些, 那些, 哪些.

counts: A small amount — "a bit of"
rule: Use with uncountable things: water, money, time, food.

examples.en: I only have a little money

trap: 一点儿 goes BEFORE the noun (一点儿水). 有点儿 goes before an adjective and means "annoyingly a bit" (有点儿贵 = a bit too expensive).

counts: Dates of the month, and numbers of rooms/sizes
rule: Spoken date and any assigned number.

examples.pinyin: jīntiān shì bā yuè jiǔ hào
nǐ de fángjiān hào shì duōshao

trap: 号 is spoken, 日 is written: a calendar prints 九日, a person says 九号.
